notes.milestones: Row id or `prefix*` to the milestone of docs/plans/rca-parity/plan.md section 6 in which the row becomes served; the longest match wins. A row t3 serve answers today keeps the milestone of its agent method: M3 re-verifies the existing rows through the real chain.
notes.targets: Every command and project mutation: `agent:<method>` (forwarded to the agent API), `state:<key>` (device state) or `t3-local` (a projection t3 serve keeps itself), per plan section 2 Commands.
notes.unrecordable: A served row no recording can show (a pty's output, a restart, a clock, an interaction no recorded set holds): a row decision with an `unrecordable` reason, or the top-level `unrecordableTests` map of `file::test` (or `file::*`) to the reason; `wf mimic coverage --by-oracle` classes it (d). A served row with neither `"oracle": "mimic"` nor this reason fails `wf mimic coverage --check` (rule served-without-oracle).
notes.decisions: Rows with a state other than pending: not-offered needs a reason and a decidedBy milestone, excluded a reason. No row is marked served here: a row is served by the evidence in t3-evidence.json: a clean or allowlisted replay of the recording (`"oracle": "mimic"`), or, with an `unrecordable` reason, a passing behaviour test and its method-hit trace (`wf mimic coverage --app t3 --traces`).
notes.reverify: Row id to why a trace hit does not serve it yet: the mapper refuses it or answers without doing it. A call that only passes by refusing never counts; remove the note in the commit that makes the answer functional and reverified through the chain.
notes.proposed: Decision 4 (hosted credentials) is the owner-confirmed (decision 7): the service holds no GitHub or GitLab token and the executor machine's own gh and glab sign-in is used. The pull-request link, unlink and watch commands are kept in the agent API's state (state:thread.pullRequests), a target the owner has not confirmed either. M12 pull request rows, owner-confirmed (decision 7): a pull request's head is read from the project's own repository (git fetch of refs/pull/N/head or refs/merge-requests/N/head into refs/rca/, never a branch), so diffFileContents and preparePullRequestThread run no host CLI; the branch a pull request gets is always t3code/pr-N/<head> (T3 uses the head's own name for a same-repository pull request, which the CLIs do not say); a review guide is a model turn over the diff on a thread of its own with the model settings name (reviewGuideModelSelection, then textGenerationModelSelection, then defaultModelSelection), kept in the agent API's state, with its run (Running, Failed) in this process only; the thread's pull request links are shown to the phone through pullRequests.linkedThreads, not through the thread shell's pullRequests list.

rpc:server.prepareTriage.reason: it starts an in-app triage of the T3 Code install itself: the server writes the session files `t3 triage` writes (its own logs, config and version under T3 home) and clones the T3 Code source from github.com/pingdotgg/t3code into its cache, then hands the phone a prompt for a scratch thread. t3-serve is not that server (it has no T3 home, logs or release to diagnose) and rca-exec has nothing of it to read; the feature would be a network clone of a third party's repository with no state of ours to triage, so there is nothing to build and prove on the executor. The phone's own fallback is the `npx t3 triage` command it offers to copy. Owner-confirmed (decision 7).

rpc:subscribeResourceTelemetry.reason: the stream is a process monitor of the T3 install itself: samples of the T3 server, its provider and terminal roots and the Electron processes (categories `server`, `provider-root`, `electron-main`, ...) taken by a protocol-3 resource-monitor sidecar, plus update state and host power. t3-serve has no such process tree and rca-exec has no process-sampling action; the one honest part, the executor host's CPU and memory, would ship with an empty process list that the phone's resource view would present as a healthy idle server. Owner-confirmed (decision 7).

command:queued-run.start.unrecordable: no recording shows it: its recorded story is labelled command:run.interrupt and the window of that label holds thread.forceStop and queue.resume, not the start of a queued run, and one listed breaking gap remains; the behaviour test thread_surface is the only check of it

command:runtime-request.respond.unrecordable: no recording shows it: the recorded interactions never reach agent method approval.answer (an answered approval needs a scripted turn that raises one, which no recorded set holds); the behaviour test thread_surface is the only check of it

command:thread.user-input.dismiss.unrecordable: no recording shows it: the recorded interactions never reach agent method input.dismiss (a dismissed question needs a scripted turn that asks one, which no recorded set holds); the behaviour test thread_surface is the only check of it

command:subagent.stop.unrecordable: no recording shows it: the scenarios call runs on a thread whose provider (codex) rca cannot drive, so turn.start fails before a subagent exists, and one breaking gap is listed; the behaviour test thread_surface is the only check of it
